ashwin: quick heads-up — I ran a microbench for a new fused variant we prototyped: 'fuse_pack_rope_paged' (QKV pack + rope and bias fused in epilogue, paged-KV path). on dev-a100 with small seq/batch it's slower than our current fused_attn.
maria: can you paste the exact env and command you used?
ashwin: env: dev-a100, CUDA 12, driver 535, gcc 11. cmd:
```
./bench --model=gpt2 --kernel=fuse_pack_rope_paged --batch=8 --seq=128 --heads=16 --d_head=64 --kv_cache=1 --kv_page_mb=64
```
median over 30 runs (nvprof summary):
- fused_attn (baseline): 2.35 ms / forward token
- fuse_pack_rope_paged (fused): 2.95 ms / forward token (+25%)
- fuse_pack_rope_paged w/o rope-fusion: 2.48 ms
- fuse_pack_rope_paged w/o bias-fusion: 2.36 ms
notes: removing rope fusion reduces the reg pressure significantly.
kevin: did you capture registers / occupancy / spills?
ashwin: yes, from Nsight (representative snapshot):
- fused_attn: regs/thread ~62, occupancy ~0.70, spills=no
- fuse_pack_rope_paged: regs/thread ~108, occupancy ~0.35, local_mem_spills=yes
so the combined epilogue fusion (rope+bias) shoots up live ranges -> regs -> spills -> lower occupancy.
maria: that aligns with prior intuition: rope ops inline expand live ranges a lot. plus paged-KV adds extra control flow (page lookups) that exacerbates TLB churn for small batches.
ashwin: kv-cache notes: even with warmed pages, the lookup & lock for non-contiguous pages still costs ~0.12 ms/call. larger batch (>=16) amortizes it but small batch/short seq suffers.
kevin: mitigation ideas:
- chooser heuristic: avoid full rope epilogue when estimated_regs > 96 OR (seq < 256 AND batch <= 8)
- paged-KV fast-path: detect contiguous page spans and bypass page-table lookup + lock
- split-epilogue: do pack+qkv in one kernel and bias/rope in a follow-up kernel when regs high
maria: propose we prioritize a runtime rule table rather than a single fused kernel. also add telemetry to know when fast-paths are safe.
ashwin: ran a quick split-epilogue prototype (bias/rope moved to second kernel): result -> 2.20 ms / token (now ~6% faster than baseline). splitting reduced registers/~eliminated spills and occupancy recovered.
perf-bot: [auto] perf artifact uploaded: s3://redwood-perf/bench/1778001234/fuse_pack_rope_paged/nsight
kevin: excellent. suggests landing a chooser + split-epilogue option instead of a heavy-handed fully-fused default.
maria: action items:
- ashwin: open WIP PR with bench flags, nsight snapshots, perf counters, and the split-epilogue toggle
- ashwin: add a kernel-chooser rule: if regs_est > 96 OR (seq < 256 AND batch <= 8) -> pick 'pack-only' or 'split-epilogue'
- infra: run a 5% dev canary for the split-epilogue paged path; alert if p95 increases >10%
- telemetry: emit kv_page_contiguous_rate and kv_page_hit_rate; only enable contiguous fast-path when contiguous_rate > 0.95 over 1m
ashwin: rough chooser pseudocode I'll include in the PR:
```
let regs = estimate_regs(kernel, cfg)
if regs > 96:
  choose('pack-only' or 'split-epilogue')
else if cfg.seq < 256 and cfg.batch <= 8:
  choose('pack-only')
else:
  choose('fuse_pack_rope_paged')
```
maria: include benchmark matrix in the PR (seq={64,128,256,512} x batch={4,8,16}) + flame graphs.
kevin: also consider a compiler pass that can shorten rope live ranges (temp var reuse) for the paged path; if doable, that may let us keep rope fused for large configs.
ashwin: WIP PR in ~3h with artifacts and canary plan. will post canary numbers after 24h.
maria: great catch, thanks for digging in. :raised_hands:
kevin: nice triage. :rocket:
